title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 67
paragraphs: Diviners are many among the Scythians, and they divine with a number of willow rods in the following manner. They bring large bundles of rods, lay them on the ground, and unroll them; then, setting each rod by itself apart, they prophesy; and while speaking thus, they roll the rods together again, and after that place them in order a second time one by one. This manner of divination they have from their fathers. But the Enareës, or “man-women,” say that Aphrodite gave them the gift of divination, and they divine accordingly with the bark of the linden-tree. Having divided the linden-bark into three strips, the man twists them together in his fingers and untwists them again, and as he does this he utters the oracle.
